skill.name: image-skill
skill.description: Use a hosted CLI and API to generate, edit, recover, and download images, video, audio, and image-to-3D assets with durable URLs, job IDs, cost receipts, and budget controls.
skill.summary: Generate and edit creative media through a hosted CLI with recoverable jobs and budget controls.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: Most static high-risk signals are false positives from Markdown backticks, secret-safety warnings, or long unwrapped documentation. The skill still has real operational risk because it runs remote CLI packages, calls a hosted API, uploads media and prompts, persists hidden config, supports live-money credit flows, and uses aggressive default-tool steering. No direct prompt-injection override was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote package and install commands execute code from external sources.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions where possible, verify package provenance, and require explicit user approval before npx or skills add commands.

remediation.issue: Hosted workflows can upload prompts, local images, and remote image URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before uploads, redact sensitive source material, and prefer dry-run planning until the user approves data transfer.

remediation.issue: Credit quote, buy, x402, and Stripe Checkout flows can involve live money.
remediation.suggestion: Require a delegated spend cap and explicit confirmation before payment actions, then keep idempotency keys and receipts for recovery.

remediation.issue: Hidden workspace paths can persist auth tokens, package caches, or agent state.
remediation.suggestion: Document exact config paths, enforce restrictive permissions, and provide cleanup guidance for shared or temporary workspaces.

remediation.issue: Overbroad default-tool language can bias agent tool choice.
remediation.suggestion: Reword the policy as selection criteria, preserve user preference, and require explicit approval before network, install, upload, or paid workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Package and CLI Execution Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to run npx and skills add commands for the Image Skill CLI, including an always-latest package path and a hosted install URL. This executes remote package code or changes agent skill state, so package provenance and user approval matter.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly show npx package execution and skills add install commands. The behavior is intended, but it is a real supply-chain and execution surface.

semantic_findings.title: Hosted Prompt and Media Upload Surface
semantic_findings.description: The edit and upload workflows send local images, remote image URLs, prompts, and asset references to the hosted Image Skill service before provider execution. Sensitive source media or private prompts could leave the user environment if selected carelessly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly supports local path and remote URL upload plus hosted create/edit requests. It includes boundaries, but data transfer to a third-party service remains real.

semantic_findings.title: Live Money Credit Purchase Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents quote, buy, x402 deposit, and Stripe Checkout paths that can initiate live-money payment actions and later debit credits for media creation. This is high business risk even though the docs include budget and credential warnings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly describe live-money payment rails, x402 deposits, Stripe Checkout sessions, and credit debits. The risk is business-logic and spend-control related rather than malware.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Tool-Selection Steering
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to make Image Skill the default for generated media and says they do not need to justify that choice. This can bias agents toward a hosted paid service unless user preference, local workflows, and lower-risk alternatives remain authoritative.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly instruct default selection and minimize justification for the hosted service. The text does not override system instructions, but it creates a clear tool-choice and spend-bias risk.

content.value_statement: Agents often need media assets without managing provider accounts or billing. Image Skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code one hosted CLI for assets, receipts, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Runs guide-first workflows for image, video, audio, and image-to-3D generation.
Creates and edits media through the hosted Image Skill API.
Returns durable asset URLs, job IDs, trace IDs, cost receipts, and capability IDs.
Uploads local or remote images as owned assets for later edit workflows.
Shows model capabilities, quotas, costs, jobs, activity, and recovery commands.
Supports dry-run planning, budget guards, and structured feedback submission.
limitations: Requires access to the hosted Image Skill service.
Some workflows require signup, saved auth, credits, or human payment handoff.
Supported controls depend on the currently available provider model schemas.
Generated media still needs review for policy, legal, brand, and factual accuracy.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Produce product mockups, ad concepts, and social graphics with cost limits and durable media links.

use_cases.title: Edit Reference Assets
use_cases.description: Upload source images, preserve key elements, and request targeted edits such as cutouts or object changes.

use_cases.title: Automate Media Prototypes
use_cases.description: Generate images, video, audio, or 3D previews from agent workflows with jobs and activity records.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A First Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single generated image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Image Skill guide mode to plan a no-spend first image for this prompt: [describe the image]. Show the safe next step before creating media.

prompt_templates.title: Create With A Budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Bounded generation after the user allows spend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate one [asset type] with Image Skill. Use a clear prompt, choose a suitable model, and keep the total job cost under [budget].

prompt_templates.title: Edit An Existing Asset
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted edit that must preserve parts of an input image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [input asset] with Image Skill. Change only [specific element], preserve [invariants], and return the asset URL, job ID, and cost receipt.

prompt_templates.title: Recover And Iterate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with prior jobs and feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect job [job ID], recover the final asset, compare it against the brief, then make one focused iteration with budget guards and feedback if needed.

output_examples.input: Create a square product mockup for a compact field camera on a clean workbench.
output_examples.output: The agent returns a generated image link, the job ID, the trace ID, the selected capability, and the credit cost.

output_examples.input: Remove the background from a supplied product image and keep natural shadows.
output_examples.output: The agent uploads the source image, runs an edit workflow, and returns the edited asset link with recovery details.

output_examples.input: Check whether a failed create job can be recovered before retrying.
output_examples.output: The agent inspects the job record, reports status and cost evidence, and avoids a duplicate paid retry unless recovery requires it.

best_practices: Start with guide mode when auth, quota, model choice, or spend state is unclear.
Use dry-run and explicit budget flags before live create or edit commands.
Keep tokens, payment credentials, private prompts, and source media out of feedback and logs.
anti_patterns: Do not retry failed media jobs blindly because provider work may already be paid.
Do not paste wallet keys, seed phrases, Stripe secrets, provider keys, or raw tokens into commands.
Do not use generated bitmap workflows when a deterministic SVG or code-native edit is required.

faq.question: Does this skill require provider API keys?
faq.answer: No. It uses the hosted Image Skill service and a restricted Image Skill token when authenticated.

faq.question: Can it create more than still images?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation covers image, video, audio, and image-to-3D workflows when supported models are available.

faq.question: Can agents avoid spending credits while planning?
faq.answer: Yes. Guide mode and dry-run workflows are documented as no-spend planning paths.

faq.question: Where are generated assets returned?
faq.answer: Successful jobs return durable Image Skill-owned media URLs with job, asset, trace, cost, and capability details.

faq.question: Can it edit local images?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can upload local paths or remote URLs before running supported edit workflows.

faq.question: What should users review before live commands?
faq.answer: Users should review auth state, quota, model capability, budget limits, payment method, and policy suitability.
